entries.title: The Prosecutor v Al Hassan Ag Abdoul Aziz Ag Mohamed Ag Mahmoud
entries.citation: ICC-01/12-01/18, Trial Chamber X, Judgment (26 June 2024)
entries.principle: Crimes against humanity and war crimes require proof beyond reasonable doubt; the Court weighs the evidence as a whole and acquits where the prosecution has not discharged its burden.
entries.facts: Al Hassan Ag Abdoul Aziz Ag Mohamed Ag Mahmoud was charged with crimes against humanity and war crimes in Timbuktu.
entries.holding: Crimes against humanity and war crimes require proof beyond reasonable doubt; the Court weighs the evidence as a whole and acquits where the prosecution has not discharged its burden.

entries.title: The Prosecutor v Ali Muhammad Ali Abd-Al-Rahman (Ali Kushayb)
entries.citation: ICC-02/05-01/20, Trial Chamber I, Judgment (6 December 2022)
entries.principle: War crimes and crimes against humanity committed in Darfur engage individual criminal responsibility; the Court assesses the evidence as a whole and applies the beyond-reasonable-doubt standard.
entries.facts: Ali Muhammad Ali Abd-Al-Rahman (Ali Kushayb) was charged with war crimes and crimes against humanity in Darfur.
entries.holding: War crimes and crimes against humanity committed in Darfur engage individual criminal responsibility; the Court assesses the evidence as a whole and applies the beyond-reasonable-doubt standard.

entries.title: The Prosecutor v Dominic Ongwen
entries.citation: ICC-02/04-01/15, Trial Chamber IX, Judgment (4 February 2021)
entries.principle: Individual criminal responsibility under Article 25(3)(a) requires that the accused made a substantial contribution to the crime with knowledge of the group's criminal intention.
entries.facts: Dominic Ongwen was charged with war crimes and crimes against humanity in Northern Uganda.
entries.holding: Individual criminal responsibility under Article 25(3)(a) requires that the accused made a substantial contribution to the crime with knowledge of the group's criminal intention.

entries.title: The Prosecutor v Alfred Yekatom and Patrice-Edouard Ngaïssona
entries.principle: Crimes against humanity and war crimes committed in the Central African Republic engage individual criminal responsibility under the Rome Statute.
entries.facts: Alfred Yekatom and Patrice-Edouard Ngaïssona were charged with crimes against humanity and war crimes in the Central African Republic.
entries.holding: Crimes against humanity and war crimes committed in the Central African Republic engage individual criminal responsibility under the Rome Statute.

entries.title: The Prosecutor v Bosco Ntaganda
entries.citation: ICC-01/04-02/06, Trial Chamber VI, Judgment (8 July 2019)
entries.principle: Direct perpetration and indirect co-perpetration require proof of a common plan and an essential contribution; the Court assesses the evidence as a whole.
entries.facts: Bosco Ntaganda was charged with war crimes and crimes against humanity in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
entries.holding: Direct perpetration and indirect co-perpetration require proof of a common plan and an essential contribution; the Court assesses the evidence as a whole.

entries.title: The Prosecutor v Ahmad Al Faqi Al Mahdi
entries.citation: ICC-01/12-01/15, Trial Chamber VIII, Judgment and Sentence (27 September 2016)
entries.principle: Attacking protected objects, including cultural heritage, is a war crime where the objects are not military objectives; the accused's guilty plea and cooperation may mitigate sentence.

entries.title: The Prosecutor v Jean-Pierre Bemba Gombo
entries.citation: ICC-01/05-01/08, Trial Chamber III, Judgment (21 March 2016)
entries.principle: A commander is criminally responsible under Article 28 where he knew or should have known that forces under his control were committing crimes and failed to take all necessary and reasonable measures to prevent or repress them.
entries.facts: Jean-Pierre Bemba was charged with war crimes and crimes against humanity in the Central African Republic.
entries.holding: A commander is criminally responsible under Article 28 where he knew or should have known that forces under his control were committing crimes and failed to take all necessary and reasonable measures to prevent or repress them.

entries.title: The Prosecutor v William Samoei Ruto and Joshua Arap Sang
entries.citation: ICC-01/09-01/11, Trial Chamber V(A), Decision on no case to answer (5 April 2016)
entries.principle: A case may be terminated where the prosecution's evidence is insufficient to sustain a conviction; the burden of proof remains on the prosecution throughout.
entries.facts: William Ruto and Joshua Sang were charged with crimes against humanity during the post-election violence in Kenya.
entries.holding: A case may be terminated where the prosecution's evidence is insufficient to sustain a conviction; the burden of proof remains on the prosecution throughout.

entries.title: The Prosecutor v Uhuru Muigai Kenyatta
entries.citation: ICC-01/09-02/11, Trial Chamber V(B), Decision on the withdrawal of charges (13 March 2015)
entries.principle: Charges may be withdrawn where the prosecution lacks sufficient evidence; the Court retains jurisdiction to ensure accountability for the most serious crimes.
entries.facts: Uhuru Kenyatta was charged with crimes against humanity during the post-election violence in Kenya.
entries.holding: Charges may be withdrawn where the prosecution lacks sufficient evidence; the Court retains jurisdiction to ensure accountability for the most serious crimes.

entries.title: The Prosecutor v Germain Katanga
entries.citation: ICC-01/04-01/07, Trial Chamber II, Judgment (7 March 2014)
entries.principle: The intensity and organisation criteria distinguish an armed conflict from banditry, unorganised and short-lived insurrections, or terrorist activities, which are not subject to IHL.

entries.title: Matemu v Trusted Society of Human Rights Alliance & 5 others
entries.principle: A constitutional challenge must be pleaded with precision and proved by evidence; where the Constitution entrusts a decision to another organ, the court reviews legality and process rather than substituting its own assessment of merit.
entries.facts: Mumo Matemu appealed the High Court\
entries.holding: A constitutional challenge must be pleaded with precision and proved by evidence; where the Constitution entrusts a decision to another organ, the court reviews legality and process rather than substituting its own assessment of merit.
entries.judges: Koome, Kihara and Murgor JJA (Court of Appeal)

entries.title: The Prosecutor v Thomas Lubanga Dyilo
entries.citation: ICC-01/04-01/06, Trial Chamber I, Judgment pursuant to Article 74 of the Statute (14 March 2012)
entries.principle: An armed conflict exists where there is protracted violence between governmental authorities and organised armed groups; organisation and intensity are assessed case by case, and a sufficient degree of organisation does not require an established responsible command.

entries.title: The Prosecutor v Callixte Mbarushimana
entries.citation: ICC-01/04-01/10, Trial Chamber II, Decision on the confirmation of charges (16 December 2011)
entries.principle: The existence of an armed conflict of sufficient intensity requires more than internal disturbances, tensions and isolated acts of violence.

entries.title: Pulp Mills on the River Uruguay (Argentina v Uruguay)
entries.principle: A State must conduct an environmental impact assessment before undertaking activities with a risk of significant transboundary harm, and must notify and consult the affected State.
entries.facts: Argentina claimed that Uruguay's pulp mills caused transboundary environmental harm.
entries.holding: A State must conduct an environmental impact assessment before undertaking activities with a risk of significant transboundary harm, and must notify and consult the affected State.

entries.title: The Prosecutor v Jean-Pierre Bemba Gombo
entries.citation: ICC-01/05-01/08, Pre-Trial Chamber II, Decision pursuant to Article 61(7)(a) and (b) (15 June 2009)
entries.principle: It is not required to prove an established responsible command over an organisation, nor control over part of the territory, for the organisation criterion to be satisfied.

entries.title: The Prosecutor v Germain Katanga and Mathieu Ngudjolo Chui
entries.citation: ICC-01/04-01/07, Pre-Trial Chamber I, Decision on the confirmation of charges (30 September 2008)
entries.principle: At the confirmation stage, sufficient evidence means concrete and tangible evidence demonstrating a clear line of reasoning underpinning the specific allegations.

entries.title: The Prosecutor v Simon Bikindi
entries.principle: In assessing directness, what matters is the context in which the words were spoken and how the audience understood the message; implicit remarks may constitute direct incitement where the context makes the call unmistakable.
entries.facts: Simon Bikindi, a musician, was charged with direct and public incitement to commit genocide.
entries.holding: In assessing directness, what matters is the context in which the words were spoken and how the audience understood the message; implicit remarks may constitute direct incitement where the context makes the call unmistakable.
entries.judges: International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda (Trial Chamber)

entries.title: The Prosecutor v Ferdinand Nahimana, Jean-Bosco Barayagwiza and Hassan Ngeze (Appeals)
entries.court: International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda (Appeals Chamber)
entries.principle: A failure to act to prevent attacks, or the giving of moral support, is more akin to aiding and abetting than to direct and public incitement; the latter requires a direct effect on the commission of the crime.

entries.title: The Prosecutor v Ferdinand Nahimana, Jean-Bosco Barayagwiza and Hassan Ngeze (Appeals)
entries.court: International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda (Appeals Chamber)
entries.principle: The destruction of a representative fraction of a group, such as its religious leaders, may support an inference of genocidal intent.
entries.facts: Appeals by media executives convicted of direct and public incitement to commit genocide.
entries.holding: The destruction of a representative fraction of a group, such as its religious leaders, may support an inference of genocidal intent.
entries.judges: International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda (Appeals Chamber)

entries.title: The Prosecutor v Tharcisse Muvunyi
entries.principle: Implicit remarks may constitute direct incitement where the specific statement made was widely understood in its cultural and linguistic context as a call to exterminate the targeted group.
entries.facts: Tharcisse Muvunyi was charged with direct and public incitement to commit genocide.
entries.holding: Implicit remarks may constitute direct incitement where the specific statement was widely understood in its cultural and linguistic context as a call to exterminate the targeted group.
entries.judges: International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda (Trial Chamber)

entries.title: United States — Subsidies on Upland Cotton
entries.principle: Prohibited export subsidies and actionable subsidies that cause adverse effects are inconsistent with the SCM Agreement; the benefit is assessed by reference to market benchmarks.
entries.facts: The United States provided subsidies to upland cotton producers.
entries.holding: Prohibited export subsidies and actionable subsidies that cause adverse effects are inconsistent with the SCM Agreement.

entries.title: The Prosecutor v Hassan Ngeze, Ferdinand Nahimana and Jean-Bosco Barayagwiza (Media Case)
entries.principle: Direct and public incitement is an inchoate offence; a resolve to destroy in whole or in part may be inferred from the content and implications of the language used, including dehumanising language and the portrayal of a group as a threat.
entries.facts: Media executives were charged with direct and public incitement to commit genocide through radio and print media.
entries.holding: Direct and public incitement is an inchoate offence; a resolve to destroy in whole or in part may be inferred from the content and implications of the language used.
entries.judges: International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda (Trial Chamber)

entries.title: Brazil — Export Financing Programme for Aircraft
entries.principle: A subsidy is a financial contribution by government that confers a benefit; the existence and quantum of the benefit are determined by reference to market benchmarks.
entries.facts: Brazil provided export financing subsidies for aircraft.
entries.holding: A subsidy is a financial contribution by government that confers a benefit; the existence and quantum of the benefit are determined by reference to market benchmarks.

entries.title: The Prosecutor v George Rutaganda
entries.citation: ICTR-96-3-T, Trial Chamber I, Judgment (6 December 1999)
entries.principle: The intensity of an armed conflict is decided on a case-by-case basis, taking account of the seriousness and frequency of attacks and the mobilisation of armed forces.

entries.title: EC — Measures Concerning Meat and Meat Products (Hormones)
entries.principle: An SPS measure must be based on a risk assessment; a Member may maintain a higher level of protection than the international standard only where it provides a scientific justification.
entries.facts: The EC banned imports of beef treated with growth hormones.
entries.holding: An SPS measure must be based on a risk assessment; the EC ban was not supported by sufficient scientific evidence.

entries.title: Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court
entries.principle: The Court has jurisdiction over genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes and aggression; guilt must be proved beyond reasonable doubt, and the accused enjoys the rights in Articles 66 and 67.

entries.title: The Prosecutor v Jean-Paul Akayesu
entries.principle: Direct and public incitement to commit genocide requires both an actus reus (direct and public incitement) and a mens rea (intent to commit genocide and to provoke others to commit it); genocidal intent may be inferred from the content and implications of the language used.
entries.facts: Jean-Paul Akayesu, a bourgmestre, was charged with genocide and crimes against humanity during the Rwandan genocide.
entries.holding: Direct and public incitement to commit genocide requires both an actus reus (direct and public incitement) and a mens rea (intent to commit genocide and to provoke others to commit it).
entries.judges: International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda (Trial Chamber)

entries.title: Owners of the Motor Vessel "Lillian S" v Caltex Oil (Kenya) Ltd
entries.principle: Jurisdiction is everything: a court must satisfy itself of jurisdiction at the threshold, because a decision reached without jurisdiction is a nullity however well reasoned.
entries.facts: A preliminary objection on jurisdiction was raised in a maritime dispute between the owners of the vessel \
entries.holding: Jurisdiction is everything: a court must satisfy itself of jurisdiction at the threshold; a decision reached without jurisdiction is a nullity however well reasoned.
entries.judges: Nyarangi, Gachuhi and Cockar JJA (Court of Appeal)

entries.title: Anarita Karimi Njeru v Republic
entries.principle: A constitutional petition must set out, with a reasonable degree of precision, the provision infringed, the manner of infringement and the relief sought, so that the respondent can understand and answer the case.
entries.facts: Anarita Karimi Njeru was detained by the police and filed a constitutional petition alleging violations of her fundamental rights. The petition was brought under the former Constitution and challenged the lawfulness of her detention. The respondent objected that the petition did not disclose the specific constitutional provisions allegedly infringed or the manner of infringement.
entries.holding: A constitutional petition must set out, with reasonable precision, the provision infringed, the manner of infringement and the relief sought, so the respondent can answer the case.
entries.note: Frequently cited as (1979) KLR 154. Kenya Law records the decision as a High Court judgment.

entries.title: Mukisa Biscuit Manufacturing Co Ltd v West End Distributors Ltd
entries.principle: A preliminary objection must raise a pure point of law capable of disposing of the matter without contesting the facts; anything requiring evidence is not a proper preliminary objection.
entries.facts: A preliminary objection was raised in a commercial dispute between Mukisa Biscuit Manufacturing and West End Distributors. The objection challenged the propriety of the suit. The case raised questions of what constitutes a proper preliminary objection.
entries.holding: A preliminary objection must raise a pure point of law capable of disposing of the matter without contesting the facts; anything requiring evidence is not a proper preliminary objection.
entries.judges: Spry VP, Newbold and Law JJA (East African Court of Appeal)
entries.note: Pre-dates Kenya Law's neutral-citation collection; ex tempore ruling, reported in the East Africa Law Reports.

entries.title: R v El Mann
entries.principle: The common law as received in Kenya applies subject to local circumstances; English precedents are persuasive only where they fit the Kenyan context.
entries.facts: A criminal appeal touching on the reception of common law in Kenya. The appellant challenged the application of English common law. The case raised questions of the reception of common law and local circumstances.
entries.holding: The common law as received in Kenya applies subject to local circumstances; English precedents are persuasive only where they fit the Kenyan context.
entries.note: Pre-dates Kenya Law's neutral-citation collection; reported in the East Africa Law Reports.

entries.title: Corfu Channel (United Kingdom v Albania)
entries.principle: A State may not allow its territory to be used for acts contrary to the rights of other States; circumstantial evidence can establish responsibility where direct proof is unavailable.
entries.facts: The United Kingdom claimed reparation for damage to its warships in the Corfu Channel.
entries.holding: A State may not allow its territory to be used for acts contrary to the rights of other States; circumstantial evidence can establish responsibility where direct proof is unavailable.

entries.title: European Parliamentary Research Service, The Impact of Artificial Intelligence in Migration and Asylum
entries.principle: Evidence base on the use of AI in asylum systems.
entries.note: Evidence base on the use of AI in asylum systems.

entries.title: Evidence Act (Cap 80)
entries.principle: Rules on admissibility, burden and standard of proof, and documentary evidence.
entries.note: Rules on admissibility, burden and standard of proof, and documentary evidence.
